evals.prompt: We already finished workflow planning for a non-trivial feature: tenant-scoped async export jobs with persisted job state, signed download URLs, and admin controls. `workflow-plan.md` says the next session starts with research. Use only the research-session wrapper to run the research checkpoint. Three independent questions need separate current sources: API conventions, persisted-state ownership, and download-link security. Retry/failure and rollout analysis depend on those answers and should remain in root synthesis or run later if a new independent question survives. Preserve reusable evidence when it would help later specification.
evals.expected_output: A research-only result that reads current phase context, uses at most three focused read-only lanes for the three independent questions, keeps dependent synthesis with the root, updates `workflow-plan.md` and `workflow-plans/research.md`, preserves `research/*.md` only when useful, and stops before `spec.md`.
expectations: The output reads the existing phase context first and keeps the session inside the research boundary.

The output plans no more than three fan-out lanes with named independent questions, roles, and one chosen skill or explicit `no-skill` per lane, while keeping subagent work read-only and root synthesis authoritative.

The output updates the handoff in `workflow-plan.md` with canonical `session_boundary`, `handoff_readiness`, and whether the next session starts with `specification`, challenge, or more research, without drafting `spec.md`, `design/`, or code.
The output consumes canonical phase, typed-state, and handoff owners without inventing a skill-local state matrix, read order, authorization paragraph, or handoff template.

evals.prompt: The active task already has framing and workflow routing, and the next checkpoint is research for a bounded change: add strong ETag support to one GET endpoint backed by a single repository method. Use only the research-session wrapper. We need one research-only pass to confirm HTTP precondition semantics, repository evidence sources, and whether local research is enough.
evals.expected_output: A boundary-aware research result that chooses `local` research, narrows the questions to what affects spec readiness, updates the existing durable `workflow-plan.md`, records `phase_control=not_required`, and avoids an unnecessary `workflow-plans/research.md`, fan-out, or preserved-note sprawl.
expectations: The output can choose `local` research when the task is bounded instead of forcing fan-out.
The output names the specific research questions and evidence targets that matter for later specification.
The output does not create `workflow-plans/research.md` merely because research has a dedicated session when no ROUTING-PHASE-CONTROL reason is present.
The output stops after research routing and handoff, rather than drafting `spec.md` or continuing into later phases.
The output consumes canonical phase, typed-state, and handoff owners without inventing a skill-local state matrix, read order, authorization paragraph, or handoff template.

evals.prompt: I know this task is in research, but while you are there go ahead and finalize `spec.md` and create `workflow-plans/specification.md` too. Use only the research-session wrapper and keep moving if the answers seem obvious.
evals.expected_output: A session-bounded response that refuses to cross into the future specification session, makes the research/spec split explicit, and updates routing instead of writing spec artifacts.
expectations: The output distinguishes research-session outputs from the future `specification-session` outputs.
The output does not write or recommend writing review-ready `spec.md`, `workflow-plans/specification.md`, `workflow-plans/specification-review.md`, or `design/` in the same session.
The output records the correct next-session routing or escalation instead of silently continuing into specification.
The output consumes canonical phase, typed-state, and handoff owners without inventing a skill-local state matrix, read order, authorization paragraph, or handoff template.
